article_title: Eclipse Foundation's Mike Milinkovich to Retire as Executive Director in 2027 After 22 Years, Search Committee Named

content_preview.title: Eclipse Foundation's Mike Milinkovich to Retire as Executive Director in 2027 After 22 Years, Search Committee Named
content_preview.summary: Mike Milinkovich announced he intends to retire as Eclipse Foundation Executive Director in 2027; a Search Committee chaired by Bosch Mobility's Florian Bankoley is seeking his successor.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Mike Milinkovich, Executive Director of the Eclipse Foundation, [announced on November 3](https://blogs.eclipse.org/post/mike-milinkovich/new-chapter-eclipse-foundation-and-i) that he intends to retire from the role in 2027, after 22 years at the helm of the open-source foundation. The announcement, posted on the Eclipse Foundation's blog under the title "A New Chapter for the Eclipse Foundation and I," was independently noted by [JVM Weekly](https://www.jvm-weekly.com/p/the-rest-of...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clean, well-structured News piece (600 words, within the 400-1200 range) using the Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis structure. The Analysis section is clearly delineated from the factual reporting above it and does not introduce new unsourced facts.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both sources were read in full from the decompressed snapshots in sources/2026-11/eclipse-foundations-mike-milinkovich-to-retire-as-executive-director-in-2027-after-22-years-search-committee-named/ (manifest.json: both status_code 200, suspicious_patterns null). source-0.html.gz is Mike Milinkovich's own post on the Eclipse Foundation's blog (meta author tag 'Mike Milinkovich'; footer 'Copyright (c) Eclipse Foundation AISBL'), dated 3 November 2026 — every direct quote in the article (grandchildren/travel motivation, 'Board's discretion' timing language, five-years-of-succession-planning claim, the developer-tools-ecosystem framing, the Jakarta EE/Adoptium/OpenHW/ThreadX/Theia/Open VSX list, the Search Committee/Florian Bankoley/Bosch Mobility sentence, the 100-employees/15-countries figure, the Europe-based-successor suggestion and 'last step' phrase, the part-time-position intention, and every FAQ quote used in 'What We Don't Know') was checked and found verbatim in the snapshot. source-1.html.gz (jvm-weekly.com, meta author 'Artur Skowronski') independently states in its PS2 item: 'Mike Milinkovich announced on November 3 that he will retire as Executive Director of the Eclipse Foundation in 2027, after 22 years, and a search committee is looking for his successor. Jakarta EE, Adoptium and Temurin all grew up under his watch' — this confirms the article's claim that JVM Weekly independently corroborated the November 3 date, the 22-year tenure, and the Jakarta EE/Adoptium/Temurin growth attribution; the quoted 'Jakarta EE, Adoptium and Temurin' phrase is verbatim. Both hosts (blogs.eclipse.org, jvm-weekly.com) were missing from config/source_allowlist.txt; added in this review's commit with justification comments per the allowlist confirmation procedure (blogs.eclipse.org confirmed as the Eclipse Foundation's own official blog; jvm-weekly.com confirmed as Artur Skowronski's named-byline, independently-operated Java/JVM newsletter, not owned by the Eclipse Foundation) — re-running chief:review after the addition cleared the warning and the automated verdict changed from APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS to APPROVE. No suspicious_patterns matches in either snapshot. Anthropic disclosure: not required - the article does not mention Anthropic, Claude, or any Anthropic-operated product.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No hallucinated quotes or misattributions found. Claim-accuracy audit (absence/quantifier scan over title/summary/body_markdown) flagged three lines: (1) the 'last step' quote in the Analysis section, verified verbatim against source-0; (2) the 'has not set a specific date... only that timing is at the Board's discretion' and Search-Committee-composition/candidate-shortlist/community-role absence claims in 'What We Don't Know', each matched against the FAQ's actual wording ('The Board will determine the timing...', 'The Board will communicate any opportunities to participate in the selection process', 'This leadership announcement does not itself change project governance, committer roles, or existing agreements') with no independent source contradicting the absence; (3) the Analysis section's characterization of Milinkovich as 'the Eclipse Foundation's only Executive Director to date' — not explicitly stated in either source, but consistent with both sources' framing (he joined in 2004, the year the Foundation was established, and neither source names a predecessor or successor-to-date); this is a subordinate, non-headline/lead claim consistent with public record and not flagged as an error. The 'after 22 years' framing in the headline and body mirrors both sources' own framing of the tenure as of the November 3 announcement, not a Herald-derived calculation.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No editorializing beyond the clearly-labeled Analysis section, which itself sticks to interpreting Milinkovich's own stated framing rather than injecting new claims.
